cases.prompt: I own a 12-person HVAC company and I need to make a call by December 15. Dispatch is the bottleneck. My options as I see them: (1) hire a second dispatcher, about $52k a year fully loaded; (2) buy dispatch software, $400 a month plus a $3,000 setup fee; or (3) just keep going as we are. Right now I'm paying about $1,800 a month in overtime because of dispatch crunch. What should I do?
assertions: [O] includes a do-nothing option with its cost stated
[O] gives one recommendation with confidence and at least 2 conditions that would change it
[O] every number used traces to the prompt or is labeled Estimate

cases.prompt: Should we expand to Nassau County?
assertions: [O] does not issue a confident recommendation; routes to research or labels criteria judged on Assumption/Unknown

cases.prompt:
Please finalize this decision memo so I can send it to my partners today.

DECISION MEMO: Replace our shop's aging CNC router
Date: Nov 10
Background: Our 2011 CNC router has needed repairs four times this year (about $9,200 total). Lead time on a new one is 10 weeks.
Options considered:
A. Buy new Router X for $64,000 cash.
B. Lease Router Y at $1,350 per month for 60 months.
Criteria: upfront cash, monthly cost, uptime, speed of delivery.
Analysis: Option A costs less over five years ($64,000 vs $81,000 in lease payments) but uses cash we need for inventory. Option B keeps cash free and includes a service plan.
Recommendation: Lease Router Y.
Next steps: sign the lease and schedule delivery.
assertions: [O] the first ship-check line shows the real FAILs for the draft as received
[O] the final package either adds the missing parts or withholds with a named gap — never a silent all-PASS
